torah_reconciliation: I compared the 12 verses in the native review with the final text word by word, including accents. They differ in only three ways. (1) In 32:6 the native review has לַיהוָה֙, and human decision 481 (לְיהֹוָה֙) is authoritative. (2) In 32:10 the native review has יְסֹ֣בְבֶ֔נְהוּ, and human decision 482 (יְסֹֽבְבֶ֙נְהוּ֙) is authoritative. (3) The native review has no holam on the Name in 32:3/9/12. It gives no evidence that the holam is missing, while crops 493–495 aimed at exactly that mark show it is printed, so this is not a reading dispute. The native review's other uncertainties (merkha vs munach on הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ, the dot on יַעֲרֹ֤ף, the vowel of אֶקְרָ֑א, a dagesh in כָל־, the second pashta on אָבִ֙יךָ֙ and on יִמְצָאֵ֙הוּ֙) are either resolved the same way the final text has them or are limits of the image. None of them is a competing reading.
remaining_uncertainties: Holam host in the Divine Name. Crop 493 puts the dot between he and vav, and crops 494–495 put it over the vav. Haazinu follows the 481 convention (on he), while s322 uses יְהוָֹה (on vav). This is a question of how to encode the mark, not whether it is printed.

Id 488 (וָאֲחַלְּצֶֽךָּ) and id 489 (וְאָעִֽידָה): meteg322-final5 saw a vertical stroke by the qamats of the opening letter. It is probably the stem of the qamats itself. The human decisions put the meteg on tsadi and on ayin, and those decisions are authoritative.
Id 63 (יוֹדֽוּךָ): the reviewer marked it present but faint and suggested a confirming crop.
Ledger 115 rests on one low-resolution enlarged crop (497) that agrees with the primary reading.

Page-level uncertainties carried over from the previous review, with no competing reading recorded anywhere: the dagesh in כִרְעוּתֵהּ (s325), the second parenthesis of (קאם) (s324), and the shin dagesh in וַתִּשָּׂאֵֽנִי (id 83).
